re timberlands in Arkansas, with closing expected in the fourth quarter • Commencing construction on first biocarbon facility in McComb, Mississippi; site selection in progress for additional locations • Monetized approximately 340,000 forest carbon credits year-to-date through third quarter; on pace for highest annual sales volume since program’s inception • Commenced construction on two additional solar sites; bringing portfolio to two operational sites and five under construction • Signed geothermal energy exploration agreement covering approximately 145,000 acres in Oregon and Washington SEATTLE , October 29, 2026 – Weyerhaeuser Company (NYSE: WY) today reported third quarter net earnings of $61 million, or 8 cents per diluted share, on net sales of $1.9 billion. This compares with net earnings of $80 million, or 11 cents per diluted share, on net sales of $1.7 billion for the same period last year and net earnings of $162 million for second quarter 2026. There were no special items in third quarter 2026. Net earnings before special items was $40 million for the same period last year and $91 million for second quarter 2026. Adjusted EBITDA for third quarter 2026 was $248 million, compared with $217 million for the same period last year and $310 million for second quarter 2026. In October, Weyerhaeuser entered into an agreement to divest approximately 81,000 acres of non-core timberlands in Arkansas for $146 million. The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter and is subject to customary closing conditions. Consistent with the company’s long-standing approach to active portfolio management, Weyerhaeuser will continue to evaluate opportunities to optimize the return profile of its timberlands portfolio, while also creating additional flexibility for broader capital allocation and growth priorities as market conditions and opportunities evolve. “Our teams delivered solid operating performance in the third quarter against an increasingly challenging macroeconomic backdrop,” said Devin W. Stockfish, president and chief executive officer. “In addition, we continued to enhance the value of our timberlands portfolio and made meaningful progress advancing several strategic growth initiatives. Looking ahead, we remain confident in the longer-term demand fundamentals that support growth for our businesses and are well positioned to navigate the current environment given the strength of our portfolio, balance sheet and flexible capital allocation framework.
